evidence.quote: Because Amazon EC2 doesn't keep a copy of your private key, there is no way to recover a private key if you lose it.
However, there can still be a way to connect to instances for which you've lost the private key.

As an alternative to key pairs, you can use [AWS Systems Manager Session Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/session-manager.html) to connect to your instance with an interactive browser-based shell or the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI).

The page says there may still be a way and names Session Manager as an alternative, but the steps are on TroubleshootingInstancesConnecting.html#replacing-lost-key-pair, which is not in the snapshot. The 'replace a public key' page and the Session Manager page are also missing. Across the 15 EC2 and Systems Manager pages, what-is-systems-manager.html is the only other relevant hit. It adds one prerequisite (SSM Agent must be installed on a managed node), but it gives no steps for a lost key. The ec2-instance-metadata.html and security-pillar mentions of EC2 Instance Connect are passing references with no instructions. So the verdict is partial.
